issues.title: Dynamic Intl locale-data import bloats the Plone bundle by ~770 lazy chunks (~340 MB on disk)

contributor_summary.summary_markdown:
## What this issue is about
This issue addresses the significant increase in the size of the Plone bundle due to dynamic imports of locale data from the `@formatjs/intl-datetimeformat` library. The current build includes approximately 770 additional lazy chunks, resulting in a bloat of around 340 MB, which is excessive for most deployments.

## What needs to be done
We need to optimize the dynamic import to limit the loaded locale data to only those languages officially supported by Plone. This can be achieved by adding a Webpack magic comment to refine which locale files to include.

## Helpful background
The problem arises from recent commits that made the dynamic imports resolvable by Webpack, resulting in every locale file being bundled, even those rarely used. Although this does not affect runtime performance for users, it unnecessarily increases the package size, complicating deployments.

## Good first steps
1. Review the current implementation in `src/core/intl-loader.js`.
2. Familiarize yourself with Webpack magic comments and the list of supported languages in `plone.app.locales`.
3. Consider the proposed changes to restrict the chunks, while also discussing alternatives such as loading locales from a static source.
4. Prepare to test the build to ensure it functions correctly with the updated imports.

Feel free to reach out for clarification if any part of the issue discussion seems ambiguous. Your contributions could help streamline Plone's bundle size significantly!

issues.title: pre-commit hook should only be run on modified files

contributor_summary.summary_markdown:
## What this issue is about
This issue addresses an enhancement for the `plone.recipe.codeanalysis` repository. The goal is to modify the pre-commit hook so that it runs only on files that have been modified, rather than on the entire codebase. This change aims to reduce unnecessary validations, making the process more efficient.

## What needs to be done
The pre-commit hook should be updated to check which files have been modified using the command:
```
git diff --cached --name-only
```
This will allow tools like Flake8, JSHint, and CSS Lint to run only on the relevant files (Python, JavaScript, and CSS respectively). Discussion around whether to retain the old way as an option is still ongoing.

## Helpful background
Currently, when committing changes, the pre-commit hook runs validations on all files, which can be inefficient. Enhancing it to target modified files could streamline the development process. A related pull request has been created to introduce this filtering.

## Good first steps
1. Familiarize yourself with the existing pre-commit hook code in the repository.
2. Review the command `git diff --cached --name-only` to understand how it identifies changed files.
3. Consider the implications of keeping the old behavior as an option.
4. Test your changes thoroughly to ensure the hook still runs appropriate checks.
